title: Preferred Painters of Gainesville Alternative for HOAs
description: HOA boards comparing Preferred Painters of Gainesville with Precision Paint Experts: the insurance, scope, and color-approval questions to settle in writing.
h1: Preferred Painters of Gainesville vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: When a community association hires a painter, the board answers to every owner. Here is a practical checklist for comparing contractors on an HOA repaint.

keywords.primary: preferred painters of gainesville vs precision paint experts
questions: What insurance should an HOA require from a painting contractor?
How should an HOA compare painting bids?

sections.h2: An HOA board's view of the comparison
body: If your association's shortlist includes Preferred Painters of Gainesville next to Precision Paint Experts, this page gives you a way to line the bids up. You will not find remarks about any other company here; it is written for directors and community managers who will have to explain the final pick at an owners' meeting.

A low number only holds up in front of owners when each proposal prices an identical scope and each contractor holds proper insurance. In other words, the documents in the packet deserve as much scrutiny as the brushwork.

sections.h2: What your board packet should contain from each painting bid
body: We cover this in more depth in a guide for associations hiring licensed, insured painters; at minimum, ask each bidder for:
bullets: A certificate of insurance listing the association by name, delivered ahead of the first work day.
Proof that each worker on site is covered by workers' compensation.
A straight answer on who employs the painters: the bidder or a sub.
An itemized scope: buildings, surfaces, prep, products, coat counts.
A written workmanship warranty and its length.

sections.h2: How Precision Paint Experts answers that packet
body: Our answers, item by item: Florida licensed and bonded, carrying full insurance, workers' comp in place for every painter, and a COI made out to your association before mobilization. The crews are our employees; no part of an HOA job is subbed out.

The proposal your manager receives separates included surfaces from excluded ones and names each prep task, the primer and finish product lines, coat counts, and the calendar. Building exteriors are backed by our written workmanship warranty for as long as 10 years, in addition to the coatings maker's warranty. Change orders cannot slip through, since any addition requires a signature in writing before it happens.

For multi-building communities, the estimate can break the work into phases so the board can see which buildings are painted in which order. That helps managers plan owner notices, parking, and landscaping schedules. Prep steps such as washing, mildew treatment, re-caulking, and rot or fascia replacement are spelled out per scope, so the board knows what owners will see crews doing before the paint goes on.

Most communities either have an approved color scheme or need owners to vote before it changes. Give us a chip or an old can from maintenance storage and we will reproduce the current scheme, then paint full-size drawdowns that directors can hold up against the buildings. Planning a refreshed look? A color consultation trims the field to a few strong schemes before it goes to the membership.

We recommend booking building exteriors for the October to May window. Residents stay in their units throughout, and because dates are part of the written proposal, the management office can post notices well ahead of each phase.

Common-area interiors such as clubhouses, mailroom areas, and stairwells can be scoped alongside the exteriors or on their own. Low-VOC options are useful when those spaces stay open to residents during the work.

sections.h2: Request a scope for your community
body: Our crew lead tours the community, measures each building, and documents its condition in photos; the itemized proposal typically lands one business day after that tour. Learn more about painting for associations and managed properties, or ask for a free estimate to put in front of the board. We also handle commercial painting in Gainesville.

faqs.q: Will you name our association on your insurance certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Before crews mobilize, we issue a COI with your association listed as the certificate holder.

faqs.q: Can you present color drawdowns to the board?
faqs.a: Yes. Directors get full-size painted samples, and current community colors can be matched from a chip or a can of leftover paint.

faqs.q: How are additional repairs handled once work starts?
faqs.a: Any repair beyond the approved proposal is written up and signed off by the association before a crew touches it.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with an HOA exterior repaint?
faqs.a: Our workmanship on community exteriors is warranted in writing for up to 10 years, and the paint manufacturer's product warranty applies on top.
